note: Bare لم is ambiguous for interrogative 'why'.
proposed_target: لماذا تعتقد أنّه يجب أن تقوم بذلك؟
proposed_english: Why do you think you have to do that?

note: لم يجب أن أفعل is not a correct expression of 'I shouldn't do'; rewrite the modal construction.
proposed_target: لم تكن تعلم أنني لا ينبغي أن أفعل ذلك، أليس كذلك؟
proposed_english: You didn't know I shouldn't do that, did you?

note: Current لِمْ changes the meaning to 'why'; intended past negation is لم. Also standard spelling is الاجتماع.
proposed_target: لم أعلم كم سيطول الاجتماع.
proposed_english: I didn't know how long the meeting would last.

note: After يعلم, أحد is the grammatical subject and should not appear as accusative أحدًا.
proposed_target: لم أشأ أن يعلم أحدٌ أين كنت.
proposed_english: I didn't want anyone to know where I was.

note: Bare لم is ambiguous; use explicit لماذا.
proposed_target: لا أعلم لماذا ينبغي أن نقوم بذلك.
proposed_english: I don't know why we have to do that.

note: Arabic says أريد سؤالك ('want to ask you'); English says 'need to ask you'.
proposed_target: لدي سؤال أريد سؤالك عنه.
proposed_english: I have a question I want to ask you.

note: أربعة أضعاف means four times as many, not the mathematically ambiguous 'four times more'.
proposed_target: لدي أربعة أضعاف ما عندك من الأقراص المدمجة.
proposed_english: I have four times as many CDs as you do.

note: أحتاج لتقول لي is ungrammatical; use أحتاج منك أن تقول لي.
proposed_target: أحتاج منك أن تقول لي أين أذهب.
proposed_english: I need you to tell me where to go.

note: Arabic is adjectival 'I am grateful', while English is verbal 'I thank you'.
proposed_target: إني شاكر لك من أعماق قلبي.
proposed_english: I am grateful to you from the bottom of my heart.

note: Arabic lacks كيف required for 'know how to do'.
proposed_target: ظننت أنّك لا تعرف كيف تفعل أيّ شيء.
proposed_english: I thought you didn't know how to do anything.

note: وقتًا أكثر is a calque; idiomatic MSA uses مزيدًا من الوقت.
proposed_target: أريد أن أقضي مزيدًا من الوقت معك وحدنا.
proposed_english: I want to spend more time alone with you.

note: Subject mismatch: Arabic says what I want to do; English says what I want you to do.
proposed_target: سأخبرك بما أريدك أن تفعله.
proposed_english: I'll tell you what I want you to do.

note: The relative clause is missing the copular link needed for 'where you told me it would be'.
proposed_target: كان في المكان الذي قلت لي إنه سيكون فيه.
proposed_english: It was where you told me it would be.

note: عشت فيها طفولتي is awkward; 'spent my childhood' is قضيت طفولتي.
proposed_target: هذه هي القرية التي قضيت فيها طفولتي.
proposed_english: This is the village where I spent my childhood.

note: Normalize conjunction spacing and use a more idiomatic expression for taste.
proposed_target: ذوقيه وأخبريني كيف مذاقه.
proposed_english: Try it and tell me what it tastes like.

note: أيمكننك is a typo; correct form is أيمكنك.
proposed_target: أيمكنك أن توصلني إلى المحطة؟
proposed_english: Can you give me a lift to the station?

note: استلم takes hamzat al-wasl, not إستلم.
proposed_target: هل استلمتَ الرسالة التي أرسلتها لكَ بالأمس؟
proposed_english: Did you receive the message I sent you yesterday?

note: Normalize Arabic على and reflect possessive أسئلتك in English.
proposed_target: هل عليّ أن أجيب على أسئلتك كلها؟
proposed_english: Do I have to answer all of your questions?

note: هذه is singular feminine ('this one') here, while English says plural 'these'.
proposed_target: هل عندك واحد أكبر قليلًا من هذه؟
proposed_english: Do you have one a little bigger than this one?

note: Correct الآن and use ذلك to match English 'that'.
proposed_target: هل تريدين حقًا التحدث بشأن ذلك الآن؟
proposed_english: Do you really want to talk about that now?

note: المدينة is feminine, so relative pronoun must be التي.
proposed_target: هل تذكر المدينة التي ولد بها؟
proposed_english: Do you remember the town where he was born?

note: Arabic says 'made a mistake on purpose' without demonstrative 'that'.
proposed_target: هل تظنه أخطأ عمدًا؟
proposed_english: Do you think he made a mistake on purpose?

note: بها is unnecessary/awkward after ركبت; use direct object.
proposed_target: متى كانت آخر مرة ركبت دراجة هوائية؟
proposed_english: When was the last time you rode a bike?

note: English declarative wording conflicts with the Arabic interrogative.
proposed_target: تقول إنك تتعمد إخفاء مظهرك الحسن؟
proposed_english: Are you saying you intentionally hide your good looks?

note: English double negative is incorrect; Arabic means neither parent knows how to swim.
proposed_target: كلا والداي لا يعرفان كيف يسبحان.
proposed_english: Neither of my parents knows how to swim.

note: Standard MSA uses في الساعة الرابعة rather than colloquial على الساعة الرابعة.
proposed_target: لقد وعدني أنه سيأتي في الساعة الرابعة.
proposed_english: He promised me that he would come at four.
